blocks.title: The Basics of Driving
blocks.body:
Driving safely starts with **understanding your vehicle** and how to control it properly.

For new drivers, the Alberta Driver’s Guide emphasizes:
- Vehicle preparation
- Smooth control
- Awareness of surroundings

Mastering the basics helps prevent accidents and builds confidence.

blocks.title: Preparing to Drive
blocks.body:
Before moving the vehicle, drivers must prepare properly.

You should:
- Adjust your seat for full control of pedals
- Adjust mirrors to reduce blind spots
- Fasten your seat belt
- Ensure all passengers are secured
- Check that doors are closed and lights are working

Good preparation reduces distractions once driving begins.

blocks.title: Using Vehicle Controls
blocks.body:
Drivers must understand basic vehicle controls, including:
- Accelerator (gas pedal)
- Brake pedal
- Steering wheel
- Gear selector (Park, Reverse, Drive)
- Turn signals
- Headlights and windshield wipers

Always know the location and function of controls before driving.

blocks.title: Steering Techniques
blocks.body:
Proper steering improves control and safety.

Recommended steering methods:
- **Push–pull steering**: keeps hands in control
- Hands positioned at **9 and 3 o’clock**

Avoid:
- Crossing arms
- One-handed steering (except when reversing)
- Sudden or sharp steering movements

Smooth steering helps maintain vehicle stability.

blocks.title: Lane Positioning
blocks.body:
Correct lane positioning helps maintain safety and visibility.

Drivers should:
- Stay centered in the lane
- Keep equal space on both sides
- Adjust position slightly to avoid hazards

Poor lane positioning can lead to sideswipes or drifting into other lanes.

blocks.title: Observing and Scanning
blocks.body:
Good drivers constantly observe their surroundings.

You should:
- Look well ahead of your vehicle
- Scan side-to-side
- Check mirrors regularly
- Be aware of pedestrians, cyclists, and other vehicles

Observation allows you to react early and safely.

blocks.title: Starting, Stopping, and Parking
blocks.body:
Basic vehicle movements must be done safely.

When starting:
- Check mirrors and blind spots
- Signal if required

When stopping:
- Stop smoothly and fully
- Leave space between vehicles

When parking:
- Secure the vehicle
- Turn wheels appropriately on hills
- Apply the parking brake

blocks.title: Common Beginner Driving Mistakes
blocks.body:
New drivers often make these mistakes:
- Not adjusting mirrors correctly
- Oversteering or understeering
- Braking too late
- Forgetting to signal
- Fixating on one object instead of scanning

Awareness of these mistakes helps prevent collisions.

blocks.title: Exam Tip: Basics of Driving Questions
blocks.body:
On the Class 7 test:
- Choose answers that show **control and preparation**
- Avoid aggressive or rushed actions
- Look for smooth, safe driving behaviors

The exam tests proper technique, not speed or confidence.

blocks.title: Handling Emergency Situations
blocks.body:
Emergency situations require **calm, quick, and correct decisions**.

For the Alberta Class 7 test, you must know how to respond safely to:
- Emergency vehicles
- Collisions
- Vehicle breakdowns
- Adverse weather conditions

Correct responses can prevent injuries, save lives, and avoid legal trouble.

blocks.title: Emergency Vehicles: What They Are
blocks.body:
Emergency vehicles include:
- Police vehicles
- Ambulances
- Fire trucks

They use:
- Flashing lights
- Sirens
- Special right-of-way privileges

All drivers are **legally required** to give them priority.

blocks.title: Responding to Emergency Vehicles
blocks.body:
When you hear a siren or see flashing lights:

- Pull over to the **right side of the road**
- Stop and remain stopped
- Do not continue driving until the emergency vehicle has passed

If you are in an intersection:
- Clear the intersection **only if it is safe**
- Then pull over and stop

Never block or follow an emergency vehicle.

blocks.title: What to Do After a Collision
blocks.body:
Being involved in a collision can be stressful.

Knowing what to do helps:
- Prevent further accidents
- Protect injured people
- Fulfill legal responsibilities

The exam often tests correct post-collision actions.

blocks.title: Steps to Take After a Collision
blocks.body:
If you are involved in a collision:

1. **Stop immediately**
2. Turn on hazard lights
3. Check for injuries
4. Call **911** if anyone is injured
5. Move vehicles off the road if safe and no injuries
6. Exchange information:
   - Name
   - Phone number
   - Licence plate
   - Insurance details

Leaving the scene is illegal.

blocks.title: Reporting Collisions
blocks.body:
You must report a collision to police if:
- Anyone is injured
- Total damage is **over $2,000**

Even minor collisions must be reported if damage exceeds the legal limit.

Failing to report can result in penalties.

blocks.title: What to Do During a Breakdown
blocks.body:
If your vehicle breaks down:

- Pull over safely
- Turn on hazard lights
- Exit the vehicle if it is safe to do so
- Stay well away from traffic

If available:
- Set up warning triangles or flares
- Call for roadside assistance or emergency help

Never stand on the roadway.

blocks.title: Driving in Adverse Weather
blocks.body:
Poor weather requires extra caution.

**Rain**
- Reduce speed
- Increase following distance

**Snow and Ice**
- Use winter tires
- Slow down
- Avoid sudden braking or steering

**Fog**
- Use low-beam headlights
- Increase following distance
- Reduce speed

Weather-related questions are common on the exam.

blocks.title: Common Emergency-Response Mistakes
blocks.body:
- Continuing to drive when emergency vehicles approach
- Stopping suddenly in traffic lanes
- Leaving a collision scene
- Standing on the road during a breakdown
- Driving too fast in poor weather

These mistakes increase danger and legal consequences.

blocks.title: Quick Test Tips for Emergency Situations
blocks.body:
Remember these key exam rules:

- Always pull **right and stop** for emergency vehicles
- Clear intersections only if safe
- Report collisions with injuries or significant damage
- Give **at least 1 metre** when passing cyclists
- Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks
- Avoid blind spots of large trucks

Choose answers that show **safety, legality, and caution**.

blocks.title: Why Intersections Matter
blocks.body:
Intersections are one of the **most common locations for collisions**.

For the Alberta Class 7 test, you must understand:
- Right-of-way rules
- Stop and yield behavior
- How to turn safely

Most exam questions are based on **simple situations**.

blocks.title: What Is an Intersection?
blocks.body:
An intersection is where **two or more roads meet**.

Intersections can be:
- Controlled (with signs or lights)
- Uncontrolled (no signs or lights)

The rules change depending on the type.

blocks.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled Intersections
blocks.body:
**Controlled intersections** have:
- Traffic lights
- Stop signs
- Yield signs

**Uncontrolled intersections** have:
- No signs
- No traffic signals

At uncontrolled intersections, **right-of-way rules are critical**.

blocks.title: Right-of-Way Basics
blocks.body:
Right-of-way means **who goes first**.

General rules:
- Yield to vehicles already in the intersection
- Yield to the vehicle on your **right**
- Yield when turning left
- Yield to pedestrians and cyclists

Never assume another driver will stop.

blocks.title: Four-Way Stop Intersections
blocks.body:
At a four-way stop:
- The first vehicle to stop goes first
- If two vehicles stop at the same time, the vehicle on the **right goes first**
- Vehicles going straight have priority over turning vehicles

Always make a **complete stop**.

blocks.title: Turning Left at Intersections
blocks.body:
When turning left:
- Yield to oncoming traffic
- Yield to pedestrians crossing
- Enter the intersection only when safe

Left turns are **high-risk** and tested frequently.

blocks.title: Turning Right at Intersections
blocks.body:
When turning right:
- Stop completely at a stop sign or red light
- Yield to pedestrians
- Yield to cyclists
- Turn only when safe

Right turns on red are allowed **unless prohibited by a sign**.

blocks.title: Common Exam Mistakes
blocks.body:
- Forgetting to yield when turning left
- Rolling stops at stop signs
- Ignoring pedestrians at intersections
- Confusing right-of-way at four-way stops

The exam tests **rules**, not driver courtesy.

blocks.title: Exam Tip: How to Answer Intersection Questions
blocks.body:
When answering exam questions:
1. Identify the type of intersection
2. Look for stop or yield signs
3. Determine who arrived first
4. Apply right-of-way rules

Do not guess — follow the rules step by step.

blocks.title: What Is a Driver’s Licence?
blocks.body:
A driver’s licence allows you to legally operate a motor vehicle.

In Alberta, driver licensing is **graduated**, meaning you gain driving privileges step by step.
This system helps new drivers build experience safely.

blocks.title: Alberta Driver’s Licence Classes
blocks.body:
Alberta has several licence classes.

The most common ones are:
- **Class 7** – Learner (written test)
- **Class 5 GDL** – Probationary licence
- **Class 5** – Full licence

Each class comes with different rules and privileges.

blocks.title: What Is a Class 7 Licence?
blocks.body:
A **Class 7** licence is a learner’s licence.

It allows you to begin driving **only under supervision** after passing the written knowledge test.

Most new drivers — including newcomers to Canada — start with Class 7.

blocks.title: Age & Eligibility Requirements
blocks.body:
To apply for a Class 7 licence, you must:
- Be **14 years old or older**
- Provide **identification**
- Pass the **written knowledge test**
- Pass a **vision test**

No road test is required for Class 7.

blocks.title: Class 7 Driving Restrictions
blocks.body:
When driving with a Class 7 licence:
- You must be accompanied by a **fully licensed (Class 5)** driver
- The supervising driver must be **18 years or older**
- **Zero alcohol or drugs** allowed
- You cannot drive between **midnight and 5 a.m.** (some exceptions apply)

These rules are strictly enforced.

blocks.title: Common Mistakes New Drivers Make
blocks.body:
- Thinking Class 7 allows solo driving
- Not understanding alcohol zero-tolerance rules
- Confusing Class 7 with Class 5 GDL
- Ignoring supervision requirements

These mistakes can result in fines or licence suspension.

blocks.title: What Is Responsible Driving?
blocks.body:
Responsible driving means being **proactive, aware, and safe** on the road.

For Class 7 learners, responsible driving is essential to:
- Avoid collisions
- Protect passengers and other road users
- Pass the knowledge test

This topic focuses on **driver behavior**, not just traffic laws.

blocks.title: Proactive Driving Basics
blocks.body:
Responsible drivers take action **before problems happen**.

This includes:
- Developing a safe and patient attitude
- Being aware of surroundings at all times
- Making good decisions early, not at the last second
- Driving defensively instead of aggressively

Good driving starts with **thinking ahead**.

blocks.title: Defensive Driving Techniques
blocks.body:
Defensive driving means preparing for the actions of others.

Key techniques include:

- **Scan ahead**
  - 12–15 seconds ahead in city driving
  - 20–25 seconds ahead on highways

- **Check mirrors**
  - Every 8–12 seconds
  - Perform shoulder checks for blind spots

- **Watch for hazards**
  - Fixed hazards: curves, intersections, parked vehicles
  - Variable hazards: pedestrians, cyclists, ice, animals

- **Keep space**
  - Use the two-second following rule
  - Increase distance in poor weather
  - Maintain space in front, behind, and to the sides

blocks.title: Planning Ahead While Driving
blocks.body:
Planning ahead reduces stress and sudden movements.

Responsible drivers:
- Signal early before turning or changing lanes
- Choose the correct lane well in advance
- Do not reverse if a turn is missed
- Continue safely and take the next available route

Late decisions often lead to collisions.

blocks.title: Impairment and Zero Tolerance
blocks.body:
For Class 7 drivers, Alberta enforces **zero tolerance** for impairment.

This means:
- No alcohol
- No drugs
- No cannabis

Any amount can result in:
- 30-day licence suspension
- Vehicle seizure
- Fines and penalties

Some medications — even over-the-counter — can impair driving.
Always read labels and avoid driving if affected.

blocks.title: Using Mobile Devices
blocks.body:
It is illegal to use a hand-held mobile device while driving.

This includes:
- Texting
- Calling
- Holding a phone

Hands-free devices may be allowed, but distractions are still dangerous.

blocks.title: Fatigue and Driver Alertness
blocks.body:
Driving while tired is dangerous.

Signs of fatigue include:
- Slower reaction time
- Drifting between lanes
- Difficulty focusing

To manage fatigue:
- Get proper sleep before driving
- Take breaks every 2 hours
- Keep the vehicle cool and ventilated
- Pull over if you feel tired

Never continue driving when alertness is reduced.

blocks.title: Passengers and Load Safety
blocks.body:
Drivers are responsible for their passengers and vehicle load.

You must:
- Ensure all passengers wear seat belts
- Never carry more passengers than seat belts
- Follow child safety seat requirements
- Secure loose items in the vehicle

Loads extending more than 1.5 metres must be marked with a red flag.

blocks.title: Common Responsible Driving Mistakes
blocks.body:
Common mistakes include:
- Following too closely
- Using a phone briefly while stopped
- Driving while tired
- Ignoring hazard awareness
- Acting aggressively toward other drivers

These behaviors increase collision risk and exam failure.

blocks.title: Exam Tip: Responsible Driving Questions
blocks.body:
On the Class 7 test:
- Choose the **safest option**
- Avoid aggressive or risky actions
- Look for answers that reduce danger
- Focus on hazard awareness and prevention

The correct answer usually shows **patience, caution, and control**.

blocks.title: Why Road Signs Matter
blocks.body:
Road signs communicate **rules, warnings, and directions**.

For the Alberta Class 7 test, you must recognize signs by:
- Shape
- Color
- Symbol

Text is often **not required** on the exam.

blocks.title: Main Categories of Road Signs
blocks.body:
Road signs fall into four main categories:

- **Regulatory** – rules you must obey  
- **Warning** – hazards ahead  
- **Guide** – directions and services  
- **Construction** – road work zones

blocks.title: Shapes & Colors
blocks.body: Each sign shape has a meaning, even without text.

blocks.title: Exam Rules to Memorize
blocks.body:
- Red signs mean **stop or prohibited**
- Yellow signs mean **warning**
- Octagon shape is **only for STOP**
- Triangle shape means **Yield**

blocks.title: Common Exam Mistakes
blocks.body:
- Confusing warning signs with regulatory signs
- Ignoring shape and focusing only on text
- Forgetting that school zones use a **pentagon**

blocks.title: Why Sharing the Road Matters
blocks.body:
Roads are shared by many types of users.

Drivers must safely share the road with:
- Pedestrians
- Cyclists
- Motorcyclists
- Large vehicles
- Public transit

The Class 7 test checks awareness of vulnerable road users.

blocks.title: Sharing with Pedestrians
blocks.body:
Pedestrians are the most vulnerable road users.

Drivers must:
- Yield at crosswalks
- Stop for pedestrians when required
- Watch for children and seniors
- Be extra cautious in school zones

Always expect pedestrians to make mistakes.

blocks.title: Sharing with Cyclists
blocks.body:
Cyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers.

When passing cyclists:
- Leave at least **1 metre** of space
- Slow down
- Do not crowd or honk

Cyclists may use traffic lanes when necessary.

blocks.title: Sharing with Motorcyclists
blocks.body:
Motorcycles are harder to see than cars.

Drivers should:
- Check mirrors carefully
- Allow full lane space
- Avoid sudden lane changes

Never assume a motorcycle is far away.

blocks.title: Sharing with Large Vehicles
blocks.body:
Large vehicles have blind spots.

Drivers must:
- Avoid driving in blind spots
- Give trucks extra space
- Allow wide turns
- Pass only when safe

Large vehicles need more time to stop.

blocks.title: Common Sharing-the-Road Mistakes
blocks.body:
- Tailgating large vehicles
- Passing cyclists too closely
- Ignoring pedestrians
- Driving in blind spots

These mistakes are dangerous and exam-relevant.

blocks.title: Exam Tip: Sharing the Road
blocks.body:
For sharing-the-road questions:
- Choose the safest option
- Protect vulnerable road users
- Give space and time

Safety is always the priority.

blocks.title: Understanding Right of Way
blocks.body:
Right of way determines **who moves first** in traffic situations.

For the Alberta Class 7 test, right-of-way questions are very common.
You must know when to:
- Proceed
- Yield
- Stop completely

Right of way is based on **rules**, not courtesy.

blocks.title: What Right of Way Means
blocks.body:
Right of way means the legal right to proceed before others.

Drivers must:
- Yield when required
- Never force their way through
- Always be prepared to stop

Having the right of way does **not** remove responsibility to drive safely.

blocks.title: Yielding to Pedestrians
blocks.body:
Pedestrians have priority in many situations.

You must yield:
- At marked and unmarked crosswalks
- When turning at intersections
- When pedestrians have a walk signal
- To people using mobility aids

Failing to yield to pedestrians is a serious offence.

blocks.title: Right of Way at Intersections
blocks.body:
General right-of-way rules include:
- Yield to vehicles already in the intersection
- At uncontrolled intersections, yield to the vehicle on your **right**
- At four-way stops, first to stop goes first
- Vehicles going straight have priority over turning vehicles

Always come to a **complete stop** at stop signs.

blocks.title: Left and Right Turns
blocks.body:
When turning:
- Yield to oncoming traffic
- Yield to pedestrians crossing
- Yield to cyclists in bike lanes

Left turns require extra caution and are tested frequently on the exam.

blocks.title: Common Right-of-Way Mistakes
blocks.body:
- Assuming others will yield
- Forgetting pedestrians during turns
- Rolling stops
- Confusing courtesy with legal right-of-way

The exam tests **lawful behavior**, not politeness.

blocks.title: Exam Tip: Right-of-Way Questions
blocks.body:
To answer right-of-way questions:
1. Identify all road users
2. Determine who must yield
3. Apply the rule strictly
4. Choose the safest legal option

Do not guess based on what feels fair.

blocks.title: Why Traffic Laws Matter
blocks.body:
Traffic laws keep **everyone safe** on the road.

They control how drivers:
- Interact with each other
- Use the road safely
- Avoid accidents and penalties

The Alberta Class 7 test focuses heavily on **basic traffic laws**.

blocks.title: Obeying Traffic Laws
blocks.body:
All drivers must obey:
- Traffic signs
- Traffic signals
- Road markings
- Police instructions

Ignoring traffic laws can lead to **fines, demerits, or licence suspension**.

blocks.title: Speed Limits and Speed Zones
blocks.body:
Speed limits are set by law and must always be followed.

You must:
- Follow posted speed limits
- Reduce speed for weather, traffic, and visibility
- Obey special speed zones

### Common speed zones
- **School zones** – lower speed during posted times
- **Playground zones** – lower speed every day
- **Construction zones** – reduced speed when workers are present

Speed-related questions are very common on the Class 7 test.

blocks.title: Seat Belts and Child Safety
blocks.body:
By law:
- All passengers must wear a **seat belt**
- Children must use approved **child safety seats**
- The driver is responsible for passengers under 16

Failure to comply results in fines.

blocks.title: Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving
blocks.body:
Alberta has **zero tolerance** for alcohol and drugs for Class 7 drivers.

This means:
- No alcohol
- No drugs
- No cannabis

Violations can result in **immediate licence suspension**.

blocks.title: Using Mobile Devices
blocks.body:
It is illegal to use a hand-held mobile device while driving.

This includes:
- Texting
- Calling
- Holding a phone

Hands-free devices may be allowed, but distractions are still dangerous.

blocks.title: Following Emergency Vehicles
blocks.body:
When an emergency vehicle approaches:
- Pull over to the **right side of the road**
- Stop and remain stopped until it passes

Never follow an emergency vehicle too closely.

blocks.title: Common Traffic Law Mistakes
blocks.body:
- Forgetting seat belt rules apply to all passengers
- Thinking speed limits are suggestions
- Using phones briefly while stopped
- Not yielding to emergency vehicles

The exam tests **legal requirements**, not habits.

blocks.title: Exam Tip: How to Answer Traffic Law Questions
blocks.body:
When answering traffic law questions:
1. Identify the rule being tested
2. Ignore what “feels reasonable”
3. Choose the option that follows the **law exactly**

The correct answer is always the **legal requirement**.

blocks.title: Why Traffic Signals Matter
blocks.body:
Traffic lights and signals control traffic flow and prevent collisions.

For the Class 7 test, you must understand:
- Signal colors
- Arrow signals
- Pedestrian signals

Misunderstanding signals can lead to serious violations.

blocks.title: Traffic Light Colors
blocks.body:
Traffic lights use three main colors:

- **Green** – Proceed if the way is clear
- **Yellow** – Prepare to stop
- **Red** – Stop completely

Drivers must obey traffic lights at all times.

blocks.title: Green and Yellow Lights
blocks.body:
Green light:
- Proceed only if the intersection is clear
- Yield to pedestrians and turning traffic when required

Yellow light:
- Means the light is about to turn red
- Stop safely if possible
- Do not speed up to beat the red light

blocks.title: Red Lights and Right Turns
blocks.body:
Red light rules:
- Come to a complete stop
- Remain stopped until the light turns green

Right turns on red:
- Allowed after a complete stop
- Must yield to pedestrians and traffic
- Not allowed if a sign prohibits it

blocks.title: Arrow Signals
blocks.body:
Arrow signals control turning movements.

- Green arrow: turn in the arrow’s direction
- Yellow arrow: prepare to stop
- Red arrow: no turn allowed

Only turn when the arrow allows it.

blocks.title: Pedestrian Signals
blocks.body:
Pedestrian signals include:
- Walking person: pedestrians may cross
- Flashing hand: do not start crossing
- Solid hand: pedestrians must not cross

Drivers must always yield to pedestrians legally crossing.

blocks.title: Common Signal Mistakes
blocks.body:
- Turning without yielding on green
- Running yellow lights
- Ignoring pedestrian signals
- Turning on red without stopping

Signal violations are heavily tested.

blocks.title: Exam Tip: Signal Questions
blocks.body:
On the exam:
- Obey signals over signs unless directed otherwise
- Yield even when the light is green
- Choose the safest legal action

Signals control traffic flow — not speed.

blocks.title: What you'll learn
blocks.body:
**In this topic you'll learn:**

- The routine to follow before every drive, and how to sit, steer, and signal
- How stopping distance works and how to brake smoothly
- How to reverse and park (parallel, angle, perpendicular, and on hills) and where parking is not allowed

The numbers in this topic come up often on the knowledge test. They're collected in the **Key numbers** table near the end.

blocks.title: Before you drive: the 5-step routine
blocks.body:
Walk around your vehicle first. Look for children, pedestrians, and anything in your path, and check the tires and for fluid leaks underneath.

Then, in the driver's seat, follow these steps **in this order**:

1. **Lock the doors.** This keeps unwanted people out and makes the doors less likely to open in a collision.
2. **Adjust your seat.** Sit at least **25 cm** from the steering wheel, with your elbows slightly bent, able to see over the wheel and reach the pedals.
3. **Adjust the head restraint.** The centre should be level with the **top of your ears**, ideally less than **10 cm** behind your head. This protects your neck in a collision.
4. **Adjust the mirrors.** Frame the whole rear window in the inside mirror. In each side mirror, you should just see a small part of your own vehicle.
5. **Fasten your seat belt.** Wear the lap belt low and snug over your hips, and the shoulder belt across your chest. You must wear it even if the vehicle has air bags.

*Driver's Guide pp. 44–45*

blocks.title: Moving away from the curb
blocks.body:
Before pulling away:

- Check that your path is clear.
- Check your inside and outside mirrors.
- **Shoulder check** your blind spot. Mirrors do not show everything beside you.

When leaving the **right side** of the road, use your **left** signal. When leaving the left side of a one-way road, use your right signal.

*Driver's Guide p. 45*

blocks.title: Steering and signalling
blocks.body:
**Hand position:** hold the wheel at about **9 and 3 o'clock**. If the wheel design doesn't allow that, use 10 and 2. Turn corners **hand-over-hand**.

**You must signal when you are:**

- moving away from the curb or a parking lane
- turning left or right
- changing lanes

Don't signal too early or too late, as either can confuse other drivers. Turn the signal off if it doesn't cancel by itself.

**Hand signals** (from the driver's window):

| Signal | Arm position |
| --- | --- |
| Left turn | Arm straight out |
| Right turn | Arm bent **up** |
| Slowing or stopping | Arm bent **down** |

*Driver's Guide pp. 48–49*

blocks.title: Stopping distance
blocks.body:
Stopping takes longer than most new drivers expect, because three things add up:

**Total stopping distance = perception distance + reaction distance + braking distance**

- **Perception:** noticing that you need to stop takes about **¾ of a second**, and often longer for new drivers.
- **Reaction:** moving your foot from the gas to the brake takes about another **¾ of a second**.
- **Braking:** the distance the vehicle travels after the brakes are applied.

The faster you go, the more ground you cover during each part. Things you control that affect stopping distance: how well you scan ahead, your alertness and fatigue, alcohol or drugs, your **speed**, and the condition of your brakes and tires.

*Driver's Guide pp. 49–50*

blocks.title: Braking smoothly
blocks.body:
- **Begin braking early.** Braking too late may not leave enough distance.
- Take your foot off the gas before you brake.
- **For a smooth stop:** just before the vehicle stops, ease off the brake slightly, then re-apply enough pressure to stop.
- **To stop quickly (without ABS):** use **threshold braking**. Brake firmly up to the point just before the wheels lock. If they lock, ease off slightly. Locked wheels mean you can't steer.

*Driver's Guide p. 50*

blocks.title: Reversing
blocks.body:
Always reverse slowly, at a **crawl or walking pace**, and only when your path is clear.

**In a straight line:**

- Put your **left hand at the top** of the steering wheel and turn slightly onto your right hip.
- Look over your **right shoulder** through the rear window, with glances to the front.
- To correct, turn the wheel **no more than a quarter turn**.

**Turning while reversing:** turn the wheel in the direction you want the **rear** of the vehicle to go. The front will swing the **opposite** way. Look over the shoulder on the side you are reversing toward.

**Rules:**

- It is **illegal** to reverse into an intersection or a crosswalk.
- When reversing out of a driveway, go into the **nearest** traffic lane only, then drive forward.

*Driver's Guide p. 51*

blocks.title: Parallel parking
blocks.body:
To park between two vehicles at the right curb:

1. Check behind you, then slow down well before the space so your brake lights warn drivers behind.
2. Stop beside the vehicle in front of the space, **rear bumpers lined up**, about **1 metre** apart.
3. Reverse slowly about half a metre, then steer **sharply right** until you are at about **45°** to the curb.
4. Straighten the wheels and keep reversing until your front bumper clears the vehicle in front.
5. Steer **sharply left** and reverse until you are parallel with the curb.

**By law, your wheels must be no more than 50 cm from the curb.**

**Leaving the space:** reverse close to the vehicle behind, signal **left**, shoulder check **left** for traffic and cyclists, then pull out.

**Getting out on the street side:** check your mirrors and shoulder check for cyclists, open the door no wider than needed, and walk to the rear of the vehicle facing traffic.

*Driver's Guide pp. 52–53*

blocks.title: Angle and perpendicular parking
blocks.body:
**Angle parking** (about 45°, common in parking lots):

- Signal, slow down, and stay about **1.5 metres** from the parked vehicles.
- When you can see along the left side of the vehicle to the right of the space, steer sharply into it.
- Stop when your front wheel **touches the curb or is within 50 cm** of it.
- Leaving: reverse slowly and **yield** to traffic. It's hard to see when backing out.

**Perpendicular parking** (90°):

- Stay about **2 metres** from the parked vehicles as you approach.
- A stall on your **left** is easier to enter, because you have more room to turn. Only enter a stall on your left **in a parking lot**, and check for oncoming traffic first.

*Driver's Guide pp. 53–54*

blocks.title: Parking on a hill
blocks.body:
**The idea:** turn your wheels so that if the vehicle rolls, it goes **away from traffic**, into the curb or off the road.

| Situation | Turn the front wheels | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Downhill** (curb or no curb) | **Right**, toward the curb or edge | The vehicle rolls into the curb or off the road |
| **Uphill with a curb** | **Left**, away from the curb | Roll back gently until the tire rests against the curb |
| **Uphill without a curb** | **Right**, toward the edge | The vehicle rolls off the road, not into traffic |

**Memory trick:** *"Up and away"*: uphill with a curb, turn **away** from the curb. Every other case, turn **right**.

Always set the **park brake**, and put the transmission in **Park** (automatic) or a low gear (manual). Parked on the **left** side of the road? Turn the wheels the opposite way.

*Driver's Guide p. 55*

blocks.title: Where you can't park
blocks.body:
**Never park:**

- on a sidewalk or boulevard
- on any part of a crosswalk, or within an intersection
- on a bridge, an underpass, or their approaches
- beside another parked vehicle (double-parking)
- where signs prohibit stopping or parking
- near street construction, or at a fire or crash scene, where you would block traffic or emergency crews

**Minimum distances:**

- **1.5 m** from a driveway, garage, or private road entrance
- **5 m** from a **stop or yield sign**
- **5 m** from a **marked crosswalk**
- **5 m** from a **fire hydrant**, measured from the point on the curb nearest the hydrant
- **5 m** from the edge of an **intersecting road**, unless parking is marked as allowed (for example, with a meter)

**Outside urban areas:** don't park on the roadway or shoulder of a primary highway unless your vehicle has broken down or there is an emergency. Wherever you park, leave room for traffic to pass, and make sure you can be seen from **60 m** in both directions.

*Driver's Guide pp. 55–56*

blocks.title: Key numbers
blocks.body:
| What | Number | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Seat to steering wheel | at least **25 cm** | guideline |
| Head restraint | centre level with **top of ears**, under **10 cm** behind your head | guideline |
| Perception time / reaction time | about **¾ s** each | |
| Wheels to curb, parallel parking | max **50 cm** | **law** |
| Front wheel to curb, angle parking | within **50 cm** | |
| Gap beside the car ahead (parallel parking) | about **1 m** | guideline |
| Distance from parked cars when angle parking | about **1.5 m** | guideline |
| Distance from parked cars when perpendicular parking | about **2 m** | guideline |
| Parking from a driveway entrance | at least **1.5 m** | **law** |
| Parking from a stop/yield sign, marked crosswalk, fire hydrant, or intersecting road | at least **5 m** | **law** |
| Visibility when parked outside urban areas | **60 m** both ways | **law** |

blocks.title: Don't mix these up
blocks.body:
- **Hill parking:** uphill *with* a curb, wheels turn **left**. Uphill *without* a curb and all downhill parking, wheels turn **right**.
- **50 cm vs 1.5 m vs 5 m:** 50 cm is wheels to the curb, 1.5 m is from a driveway, and 5 m is from a hydrant, stop/yield sign, crosswalk, or intersecting road.
- **Reversing:** steer toward where you want the **rear** to go, because the front swings the other way.
- **Smooth stop vs quick stop:** for a normal stop, ease off the brake just before stopping. For a quick stop without ABS, use threshold braking, firm but not locked.
- **Leaving the right-hand curb:** use your **left** signal and shoulder check **left**, because traffic comes from your left.
